inputs.text: Tens of thousands marched in central London under an “anti-far-right” banner, backed by trade unions, anti-racism groups and Muslim representative bodies. With local elections approaching, the timing looks like an effort to set the boundaries of acceptable opinion before voters have their say. Branding dissent as “far-right” is no substitute for answering people’s concerns about national identity, social order and the traditions that bind communities together. A healthy society should defend open debate, not use political labels to shut it down.
